We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps are (forward) 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: start from target, break amide to carboxylic acid + amine (step1 reverse of coupling). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (reverse of Doebner). Then break sulfonamide to amine + sulfonyl chloride (reverse of sulfonamide formation). So we need propose precursors: final target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl with side chain (C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So step3: disconnect sulfonamide bond: give sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and amine (the other aromatic ring with side chain). The amine is the aniline attached to the side chain (the phenyl with C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group and to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So the amine precursor is the aniline (c2ccc(... )cc2) with the side chain still attached (the side chain includes the α,β-unsaturated amide). So step3 precursors: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (SMILES: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) and the amine: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (with an NH attached to sulfonyl? Actually the amine is the aniline: the nitrogen attached to sulfonyl is part of the aromatic ring; the SMILES for the amine would be Nc2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., aniline). So precursor SMILES: Nc2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Step2: break the α,β-unsaturated amide to aldehyde + malonic acid? Wait Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid. In our target, we have α,β-unsaturated amide (C=C-C(=O)N...). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. That's an α,β-unsaturated amide, not acid. But the forward Doebner modification yields unsaturated acid, then coupling to amine gives amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide to acid (step1) gave unsaturated acid. Then step2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So the unsaturated acid precursor is: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the acid SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (with the same phenyl). Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl ring via the double bond: the phenyl ring is attached to the double bond carbon (beta carbon). So the acid precursor: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2. Then step2 precursors: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde would be the same phenyl ring with aldehyde at the position where the side chain attaches: the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring at the same position as the side chain (para? Actually the side chain is attached at position 1 of phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So aldehyde SMILES: O= Cc2ccc(cc2)?? Wait need correct: aromatic aldehyde attached to phenyl ring: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (i.e., benzaldehyde). But our phenyl is substituted with the side chain at position 1; the aldehyde would be at that position. So the aldehyde is 4-methyl? No, it's just phenyl with aldehyde. So SMILES: O= Cc1ccccc1 (benzaldehyde). However the phenyl also later attaches to sulfonamide? No, the phenyl with side chain is separate from the tolyl sulfonyl part. So the aldehyde is just benzaldehyde (c1ccccc1C=O). Good.

Thus step2: benzaldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid attached to phenyl (c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc1). So we need template for Doebner modification. Search for functional groups broken: C-C double bond formed? Actually forward forms C=C double bond, breaks C-C bond (between malonic acid carbon and carbonyl?) and C-O bond. So we need template that breaks C-C double bond? In retrosynthesis we need to break the double bond to get aldehyde + malonic acid. So functional_groups_broken: C-C double bonds? Actually forward forms C=C, so retrosynthesis breaks C=C. So we can search for templates that break C-C double bonds and form aldehydes and carboxylic acids. Let's try search.
